note: My 1…Nc6 system. Moves checked with Stockfish 19 lite (depth 16) and counted in my own games. Built by tools/build-nc6.mjs.

plans.text: Locked centre: …Ng6 and …Nf6, …Be7 or …Bc5, …d6 and castle, then …Nh5 and …f5 (or …Nf4). Your play is on the kingside; leave the queenside to White.
White gave up the centre: develop fast with …Nf6, …Bc5 or …Bb4+, …d6 or …d5, castle short. Aim your bishop at the weakened a7–g1 diagonal and e3.
Hold e5 with the pawn on d6: …Nf6, …Be7, …O-O, …Re8. If White pushes d5, it is your locked-centre plan (…Ng6, …Nh5, …f5). Take on d4 only when it wins time.
Old Steinitz: keep the e5 pawn, …Nf6, …Be7, …O-O, …Re8 and …Bf8. The pin is harmless once the bishop on d7 covers c6.
Queens off, but nothing is wrong: …f6 or …Bd6 holds e5, the king guards the centre from e7 or c7, and …Be6, …Nge7, …Rd8 finish development.
Schliemann: the f-file is yours. …fxe4, …Nf6, …Bc5 or …Bd6, castle short and bring a rook to f8; White's e4 and f2 are the targets.
Quiet Italian: …Be7, …Nf6, …O-O with the pawn on d6. If Ng5 ever hits f7, …O-O covers it; later …Na5 trades White's best bishop.
Four Knights: keep the …d6 / …e5 chain; …Be7, …O-O, …Re8. Against Bb5, …Bd7 unpins; against d4, recapture to keep the centre closed where you can.
Against the Vienna: develop and hit e4 (…Nf6), trade White's light-squared bishop with …Na5 when it lands on b3 or c4, castle short and break with …d5.
After …exf4 you are a pawn up: develop (…Nf6, …d6, …Be7), keep the f4 pawn while it costs nothing, and castle short. White's king is the weak one.
Knight Tango into a King's Indian centre: …e5, and if d5 then …Ne7, …Ng6, …d6, …O-O and …Nh5/…f5. If White exchanges on e5, your pieces get the e5 square.
Here you take on d4 because it wins time: …Bb4 pins c3, …Ne5 hits c4, then …O-O and …Re8 against e4.
